reason: The cited evidence (E2) shows that MA and SPS can produce a CoCrFeMnNi HEA with fine grains, supporting the feasibility of the baseline and processing route, but it does not address Y2O3 addition, dispersion quality, or high-temperature mechanical properties. E1 is about a different alloy (Al0.7CoCrFeNi) and processing, providing no support for any key premise. Thus, the specific claims about Y2O3 dispersion, its strengthening mechanism, and the predicted high-temperature improvements are unsupported by the cited passages.
premises: Nanosized Y2O3 particles can be uniformly dispersed in a CoCrFeMnNi HEA matrix via mechanical alloying and SPS.
A uniform dispersion of nanoscale Y2O3 particles acts as obstacles to dislocation motion and pins grain boundaries.
This dispersion strengthening mechanism improves yield strength and creep resistance at temperatures above 800°C.
The baseline CoCrFeMnNi HEA can be produced by powder metallurgy (MA + SPS) without Y2O3.
